# SQC Analysis — Tablet Weight

Statistical Quality Control (SQC) analysis on tablet weight data.

## Project files

- `sqc_analysis.R` — main R script (loads `qcc`, `ggplot2`, `dplyr`, `forecast`, `moments`)
- `sqc_analysis.Rmd` — full analysis report (generates plots into `output/`)
- `data/tablet_weight.csv` — dataset
- `output/` — plots and results generated by the Rmd
- `renv.lock` — records the exact package versions used (for reproducibility)

## How to reproduce

This project uses renv to pin package versions. The renv.lock file records the exact versions of every package used. Running renv::restore() rebuilds that environment on your machine.

1. Clone this repository.
2. Open the project in RStudio (the `.Rproj` file).
3. Run `renv::restore()` in the Console — this installs the exact package versions recorded in `renv.lock`.
4. Knit `sqc_analysis.Rmd` to regenerate the plots and reports.

## Requirements

- R 4.3.1 (as pinned in `renv.lock`)
- Direct packages: qcc, ggplot2, dplyr, forecast, moments
- All dependencies are restored automatically by `renv::restore()`

## Project Description

This project evaluates whether a tablet compression process is **stable** (predictable) and **capable** (meets specifications). The data are split into Phase I (n = 100, calibration) and Phase II (n = 37, monitoring). An I-MR chart for individual data shows many out-of-control points, so autocorrelation and normality are diagnosed. An ARIMA model removes the autocorrelation, and an EWMA chart on the residuals is used for monitoring because it is robust to non-normal data. Finally, capability indices are computed and the process is classified.
